newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-U.S. ATHLETICS CHIEF CASSELL'S CONTRACT NOT RENEWED.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-U.S. ATHLETICS CHIEF CASSELL'S CONTRACT NOT RENEWED.

text.p: Ollan Cassell's controversial 31-year reign as U.S. athletics czar neared an end Tuesday when the sport's U.S. governing body voted not to renew his contract when it expires in 1998.

The 52-34 vote by USA Track and Field's board of directors brought to a climax years of bickering over the leadership and marketing skills of the 59-year-old Cassell, who frequently had envisioned himself as Italian Primo Nebiolo's successor as world athletics chief.

"It's time to have a healer and not a divisive element at the top," said Atlanta Track Club director Julia Emmons after the decision not to extend Cassell's contract as USA Track and Field's executive director.

Cassell, a vice president of the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) since 1984, called the outcome "not what I expected," but said he would cooperate with the group in its search for a new leader.
